full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi issue calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the failure of Respondents to take into account the full tenure of service of the Petitioner from the date of his appointment under development project of Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) of Respondent No. 1 in order to determine the Petitioner's salary and/or other incidental or associated financial benefits, including Petitioner's entitlement to Selection Grade in his service, in compliance with order dated 10-4-2013 passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 308 of 2013 and Judgment and order dated 14-5-2012 passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 8983 of 2011 (Annexure-A and A-1) shall not be declared to have been without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the Respondents shall not be directed to take into account the full tenure of service of the Petitioner from the date of his appointment under the development project of LGED of Respondent No. 1 so as to provide salary and/or other incidental or associated financial benefits, including the 5th (Fifth) Selection Grade, to the Petitioner and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper." 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why clause (Umo) of the Notification No. 46.067.010.00.00.007.2010-711 dated 5-10-2010 issued by the Respondent No. 5 referring to rule 8 of the LGED (Officers and Employees) Recruitment Regulations, 2009 (Annexure-C) so far as it relates to the Petitioners' regularization from development project to revenue budget (Annexure-C) shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and also as to why a direction shall not be given to the Respondents to pay selection grade as per rule 7(7) of the National Pay Scale 2009 

 (জাতীয় বেতন স্কেল, ২০০৯) as well as per the Notification bearing এস, আর, ও নং ৬৫-আইন/৯৫/সম/বিধি-১/এস-৬/৯৪ তাং ২-৫-১৯৯৫ 29170 এস, আর, ও নং ১৮২-আইন/২০০৫/সম/বিধি-১/এস-৯/ dated 20-6-2005 respectively counting the service period of the Petitioners from the date of joining in the development project and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the Rule 8 of the Local Government Engineering Department (Officers and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 2009 (Annexure-A) (the Rules 2009) vis-a-vis. regularization/confirmation of probationers under LGED, so far as it relates to the Petitioners who were absorbed and regularized under revenue budget from development projects, shall not be declared to be ultra vires the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, and as to why the imposition of provisions pertaining to probationers upon the Petitioners as contained in Clause No. Uma of the Respondent No. 1's Notification being No. 46.067.010.00.00.007.2010-711 dated 5-10-2010 (Annexure-A-1) shall not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and as to why the Respondents shall not be directed to take into account the full tenure of service of the Petitioners from the date of their joining under development projects of LGED of Respondent No. 1 so far to provide the Petitioners with salaries, selection grade, time scale, pension, leave and/or other incidental or associated benefits in the service and/or pass such other or further-order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why rule 6 of the “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেট স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” (Annexure-A) shall not be declared to be discriminatory and ultra vires as being conflicting with Articles 27, 28, 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh so far the appointment of Respondent Nos. 8, 9 and others dated 5-10-2010 are concerned vide Annexure-A-1 and also as to why they shall not be directed not to pay further and to take step to realize the excess public money back which they paid to Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and other similarity situated Assistant Engineers appointed under the Local Government Engineering Department (Officers and Staffs) Recruitment Rules, 1986 or 2009 respectively vide Memo dated 5-10-2010 (Annexure-A-1) “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেট স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” (SRO) (Annexure-A) shall not be declared to be not applicable in respect of Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and other similarly situated Assistant Engineers appointed under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 or 2009 respectively and that they are not entitled to receive any benefit thereunder and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 6. It is to be noted that the Petitioners in both Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 and Writ Petition No. 10664 of 2013 are represented by Mr. Mohammed Mutahar Hossain. In representing both sets of Petitioners, Mr. Hossain has treated Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 as the lead case in which he has made extensive arguments on legal issues common to both cases and has declared to this Court that he intends to adopt his arguments in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 for Writ Petition No. 10664 of 2013. Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 is distinguishable from Writ Petition No. 10664 of 2013 (and indeed from the related Writ Petition No. 6591 of 2014) in that it is only here that the Petitioners have challenged the constitutionality of rule 8 of the Local Government Engineering Department (Officer and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 2009 or LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009. This Court's consideration and evaluation of Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 has hereinafter accordingly proceeded on the basis that it is only in this Writ Petition that the Petitioners have raised an issue of constitutional law, i.e., the vires of rule 8 as permits of judicial review going strictly by the ratio decidendi in Bangladesh vs. Sontosh Kumar Saha reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94 as bears upon the extent and scope of jurisdiction of Administrative Tribunals by reference to article 117 of the Constitution. The salient elements of the ratio in the Sontosh Kumar Saha Case are thus: 

 b) infringement of fundamental rights in which case also, there must be sufficient pleadings of such violation keeping in mind that such plea also can be taken in the tribunal because the constitution being the supreme law of the country, it can be taken in aid by any court/tribunal. 

 7. Accordingly, Writ Petition No. 10664 of 2013 and Writ Petition No. 6591 of 2014 at the outset are found not to be maintainable per se by reason and application of the Appellate Division's judgment in Bangladesh vs. Sontosh Kumar Saha reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94. It is to be noted further at this juncture that no independent submissions have been made by the learned Advocate for the Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 6591 of 2014 before this Court in the course of these proceedings. 

 or Local Government Engineering Department (Officers and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 2009 ("LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009") so far it relates to the Petitioners shall not be declared to be ultra vires the Constitution and why imposition of rule 8 upon the Petitioners as reflected in clause “ঙ” (“Uma”)of the appointment Notification dated 5-10-2010 shall not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the Respondents shall not be directed to take into account the full tenure of service of the Petitioners from the date of their joining in the development project so as to provide them with commensurate salaries, selection grade, time-scale, pension leave and other benefits. 

 11. The Petitioners herein impugn the vires of rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 vis-a-vis. regularisation/confirmation of probationers under LGED so far as it concerns the Petitioners who were absorbed and regularised under revenue budget from development projects. The Petitioners further impugn the imposition of provisions pertaining to probationers under rule 8, clause Uma of the Respondent No. 1's Notification being No. 46.067.010.00.00.007.2010-711 dated 5-10-2010. The Petitioners further seek direction upon the Respondents to take into account the full tenure of service of the Petitioners from the date of their joining under development projects of LGED of Respondent No. 1 so as to provide the Petitioners with salaries, selection grade, time-scale, pension, leave and/or other incidental or associated benefits in the service. 

 12. The Petitioners as represented by learned Advocate Mr. Mohammad Mutahar Hossain, state that they were appointed/regularized in the revenue budget vide Notification dated 5-10-2010 by operation of a High Court Division Judgment in a great number of cases, 100 to be precise, disposed of analogously on 16-3-2006 (Writ Petition No. 1522 of 2004 and other related cases) directing the Respondents to absorb/regularize them in the revenue budget of the LGED in the same manner as has been done in the case of previously regularized 95 Assistant Engineers upon relaxing certain recruitment provisions of the LGED (Officers and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 1986 ("LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986"). That Judgment of 6-3-2006 covered Writ Petitions as also filed by the present Petitioners in 2004-2005 relying upon a Gazette Notification dated 28-7-2004 concerning those earlier 95 Assistant Engineers to whom then applicable rule 7 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 was made mandatorily applicable. It is noted that the terms of that previous rule 7 now corresponds to the present rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009. The operative part of the Judgment dated 16-3-2006 as relied upon by the present Petitioners reads thus: 

 13. It is stated that the LGED has, since 1988, consistently absorbed/regularised personnel working under its development projects to permanent posts under its Revenue Head as and when such posts have been created, become available or fallen vacant. The absorption/regularisation from development project to the revenue head by LGED is a matter of long-standing policy and regular practice, which is clear and unambiguous from the previous conduct of LGED. 

 14. In view of the Judgment dated 6-3-2006, the Respondent No. 1, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives by the Notification being No. 46.067.010.00.00.007.2010-711 dated 5-10-2010 absorbed and regularised the personnel, including the Petitioners, from development projects into revenue head/budget of LGED. However, as it is contended, the impugned clause Uma of the Notification dated 5-10-2010 unlawfully stipulates that the Petitioners will have to fulfill the formalities of rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009. 

 15. Rule 8 notably imposes certain requirements for probationers appointed on a temporary basis. It is the Petitioners' contention that they were initially appointed under the development projects of LGED at various dates from 1990 to 1999 and, subsequently, they were absorbed and regularised under revenue head from development projects. Accordingly from the Petitioners' perspective, such absorption and regularisation under revenue head upon working under development project since long militates against them being treated as mere probationers under LGED. Given that the Notification dated 5-10-2010 clearly and unequivocally provides that the Petitioners have been regularised under revenue head, there is no justifiable ground for clause Uma to feature in such Notification. 

 16. Furthermore, the Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 stress that clause Uma also infringes the provisions of the Determination of Regularisation and Seniority of Personnel Transferred/Absorbed from Development Project to Revenue Head Rules, 1995 ("the Rules 1995") and the Determination of Regularisation and Seniority of Personnel Transferred/Absorbed from Development Project to Revenue Head Rules, 2005 ("the Rules 2005"). Accordingly, the insistence on the continued application of clause Uma in the Petitioners' case is submitted to create an unlawful impediment in counting the tenure of the Petitioners under development projects for assessment of their salaries, selection grade, time-scale, pension, leave, and/or other incidental or associated benefits in their service. 

 17. In this context, is noted that a Writ Petition being No. 8983 of 2011 was earlier filed by some personnel impugning the concerned authorities' refusal to count the seniority of the aforesaid Writ Petitioners from the date of joining under development projects so as to determine their salaries and/or other incidental or associated financial benefits, including their entitlement to Selection Grade in the service in accordance with the Rules, 2005, Whereupon the Court by a Judgment and Order dated 14-5-2012 made the Rule absolute and directed the Respondents "to count the seniority for the salary and other benefits including time-scale and selection grade of the Petitioners from the date of joining in the development head within 60 (Sixty) days". The Respondents in Writ Petition No. 8983 of 2011 resultantly filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 308 of 2013 before the Appellate Division leading to the Order of disposal dated 10-4-2013 with the observation inter alia that the term "associated benefits" shall not only mean selection grade, but also include time-scale. 

 18. The learned Advocate for the Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014, Mr. Mohammed Mutahar Hossain draws this Court's attention to the fact that both the Rules 1995 as contained in Notification dated 2-5-1995 and, the Rules 2005 as contained in Notification dated 20-6-2005 had earlier determined the procedure for absorbing/regularising personnel from development project into revenue head as well as provided the provisions for assessment of their salaries and/or other financial benefits. Rule 5 of the Rules 1995 as well as rule 6 of the Rules 2005 provide, inter alia, that the tenure under any development project shall be counted for assessment of an absorbed/regularised personnel's entitlement to salary, leave, pension and/or other incidental or associated benefits in his service. It is noted that the vires of rule 6 of the Rules 2005 has been challenged in Writ Petition No. 295 of 2015. 

 19. Mr. Mohammed Mutahar Hossain submits that the Respondent have been deliberately ignoring the fact that the Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 are not probationers since the Petitioners have been regularised under revenue head by the Notification dated 5-10-2010 and, accordingly, the Petitioners' appointment have not been made on temporary basis. Mr. Hossain explains that, a probationer's appointment letter/notification always clearly states that his/her appointment is being made on temporary basis. By way of illustration, Mr. Hossain refers to various notifications appointing probationers against various posts of LGED clearly signifying that the probationers were appointed on temporary basis. 

 20. Mr. Hossian now submits that the impugned rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 is ultra vires the Constitution in so far as it relates to the Petitioners and the impugned provision as contained in clause Uma of the Notification dated 5-10-2010 is without lawful authority and of no legal effect inasmuch as the Petitioners, having rendered their services under various development projects since long and having been regularised vide the Notification dated 5-10-2010, cannot be classified as "probationers" and, as such, rule 8 is discriminatory in nature in so far as it relates to the Petitioners, who have been absorbed and regularised from development project into revenue head and also because the Petitioners are being treated at par with other fresh recruitees/probationers upon ignoring the long service record/tenure of me Petitioners under the development projects. He proceeds to assert further that rule 8 and clause Uma infringe the fundamental rights of the Petitioners and create impediments in counting the full tenure of service of the Petitioners from the date of their joining under development projects notwithstanding the fact that rule 5 of the Rules 1995 as well as rule 6 of the Rules 2005 oblige the Respondents to take into consideration the full tenure of the Petitioners' service under development projects and, as such, the Respondents may be directed to provide the Petitioners with appropriate selection grade in accordance with law. 

 21. By filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014, the Added Respondent Nos. 7-9 state that in 2004, 95 Assistant Engineers of the development projects were first regularized vide Gazette Notification dated 28-7-2004 on humanitarian ground upon relaxing rules 4(1), 4(3), 4(4) and column 3 of the Schedule of the direct recruitment provision of the Local Government Engineering Department (Officers and Employees) Recruitment Rules, 1986, i.e., LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 by a special dispensation involving a relaxation of their age by the Hon'ble President of the Republic as it was not possible to regularise them under the then উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেট স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করণ বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৫ or the Rules 1995. Thereafter, following the regularization of those 95 Assistant Engineers in the aforesaid manner the Writ Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 as well as their similarly placed colleagues filed 100 Writ Petitions on the ground of discrimination and the High Court Division by a Judgment dated 16-3-2006 disposed of all those Writ Petitions with a direction upon the authorities to absorb them with revenue budget in the same way as has been done in the case of regularization of 95 Assistant Engineers and accordingly the Writ Petitioners and their colleagues were regularized in the same way vide the Notification dated 5-10-2005 which says— 

 24. It is submitted by learned Advocate Mr. M.A. Gaffar on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 7-9 that in spite of being regularized under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 by operation of the Judgment dated 16-3-2006 the Petitioners in this present Writ Petition curiously claim that their regularization was made under the set of rules determining the conditions and procedures of transfer from development projects to the revenue budget known as রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ নীতিমালা, ২০০৫ notified through SRO No. 182 on 20-6-2005 or the Rules, 2005 which runs wholly contrary to their own appointment-Notification dated 5-10-2010. Significant still, and also contrary to the Judgment dated 16-3-2006, the Petitioners further claim that rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 is ultra vires in a manner that is self-contradictory with their own Writ Petitions before the earlier High Court Division Bench inasmuch as they filed their earlier Writ Petitions relying on the Notification dated 28-7-2004 incorporating rule 7 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 which at that material time was of mandatory application and which has now been replaced by the fresh yet similar provisions of rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rues, 2009. 

 25. The learned Advocate Mr. MA. Gaffar further submits that the Petitioners filed the present Writ Petition after already serving 4 years in the revenue post of the LGED seeking further the inclusion of their full tenure of service under the development projects from their respective dates of joining in the development projects in order to secure 7th selection grade, time-scale, pension and other benefits. 

 26. The added Respondents' case as made out in their Affidavit-in-Opposition and supplement aries filed is that they are 5-15 years senior in service to the Petitioners. They were earlier also in the development projects of the LGED with some of them being employed with the Petitioners in the same projects and some in other projects. While they were in the development projects, the said added Respondent Nos. 7-9 in response to a circular published by the Public Service Commission (PSC) successfully participated in competitive exams and were regularly appointed under LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986. On the other hand, the Petitioners, many of whom were unsuccessful in the PSC exams remained in the development projects. But since their projects were not completed as mandatorily required before regularization they could not aim for regularization under the then existing set of rules governing transfer from development projects to revenue budget notified through SRO No. 65 on 2-5-1995 i.e., the Rules 1995. As a result the Petitioners subsequently took advantage of a special route in the form of a special case of regularization of 95 Assistant Engineers vide Notification dated 28-7-2004 and relying on that Notification as a precedent joined forces with others similarly placed to file as many as 100 Writ Petitions with a prayer to regularize them as Assistant Engineers in the revenue budget in the same way as has been done in the case of those 95 Engineers on humanitarian grounds. That reliance on that special instance of regularization under the Notification dated 28-7-2004 paid off and their prayer was allowed by the High Court Division by the Judgment dated 16-3-2006 after analogously hearing 100 Writ Petitions. 

 27. Mr. Gaffar emphasizes that the Petitioners being fully aware of the requirement of law instead of seeking to be regularized under the then existing Rules 1995 sought to be regularized by relying on Notification dated 28-7-2004 as because they knew that like the previously regularized 95 Engineers they had also no scope to seek regularization under the Rules 1995 as their projects remained incomplete and their posts were not transferable to the revenue budget. Citing the similar case of the 95 Assistant Engineers, Mr. Gaffar explains that since their tenure of development projects was not completed the authority could not regularize these earlier 95 Assistant Engineers under the Rules 1995. With a view to resolving the resultant situation as a one-off and exceptional case the authority sought intervention of the Hon'ble President of the Republic to accommodate these disgruntled Assistant Engineers and as a result the Hon'ble President exceptionally relaxed certain recruitment provisions of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 excepting, among others, rule 7 (corresponding to the impugned rule 8 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009). Rather, Mr. Gaffar stresses, rule 7 was made mandatorily applicable through the Notification dated 28-7-2005. The present Petitioners having relied earlier on at the time of absorption upon the said Notification, Mr. Gaffar argues, and, as such, they having accepted the mandatory application of and compliance with rule 8 (as the successor provision to rule 7) and being apparently appointed under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009, they have now no locus standi to challenge rule 8 as ultra vires the Constitution. Mr. Gaffar makes it a point to add that the Added Respondents and many other officers similarly placed were also appointed by regular course as Assistant Engineers under the Recruitment Rules of the LGED and complied with the provisions of rule 8 despite the fact that they also served in development projects for 5-15 years before they entered into the service of the LGED under revenue budget, thereby negating any justifiable reason why the Petitioners should be treated any differently. 

 28. Accordingly, this Court is asked to appreciate, both the Petitioners as well as the Added Respondents being earlier in the development projects and subsequently being appointed in the LGED under the same Recruitment Rules of LGED as stated above are similarly situated and, as such, the Petitioners are not entitled to any special benefit/benefits as prayed for to the detriment of the added or anybody else similarly placed for that matter, because believing and acting otherwise will be discriminatory and in clear contravention of the fundamental rights of the Added Respondents and those others in like position guaranteed under articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution as well as go against the ethos of articles 19 and 20 fundamental principles spelt out in the Constitution. 

 29. Having heard at length both Mr. Mohammad Mutahar Hossain and Mr. MA. Gaffar and considered the pleadings and documents on record, this Court finds at the outset that the 12 Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 have sought continuously to navigate through the complex web of successive service rules and practices and have thus far been fairly successful to leverage the same to their optimum advantage. This Writ Petition is to be seen as a continuation of that long sustained endeavour on the Petitioners' part. 

 30. Evidently the Petitioners instead of seeking to be regularized under the Rules 1995 as was then in force sought to be absorbed instead by relying upon and taking advantage of the precedent set by previously regularized 95 Assistant Engineers vide Notification dated 28-7-2004 conditional upon rule 7 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 (corresponding to the succeeding rule 8 of the Rules, 2009) being mandatorily applicable. From the Gazette Notification dated 28-7-2004 it is clear that rule 7 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 was not relaxed while rules 4(1), 4(3), 4(4) and the 30-year age limit in column 3 of the Schedule were specifically relaxed by the Hon'ble President and, as such, by accepting application of rule 7 of the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 as mandatorily applicable at the time of seeking regularization before this Court in the earlier instance the Petitioners are now estopped from raising any question challenging the applicability of rule 8 corresponding to clause "Uma" of their appointment Notification of 5-10-2010. 

 31. This Court has been apprised importantly that out of the present 12 Petitioners 9 individuals have already complied with the provision of rule 8 and, as such, it is evident that all employees, including the previous 95 Assistant Engineers and the added Respondents, have been regularized after completion of their projects upon due compliance with rule 8, but for 3 remaining Petitioners. Mr. Gaffar has satisfactorily argued that these remaining 3 Petitioners cannot now be treated to be an exception to the prescribed mandatory practice without any legal basis and, as such, rule 8 being mandatory for all cannot be declared ultra vires. This Court is convinced that since the Notification dated 28-7-2004 relied upon by the Petitioners at the time of the substantive hearing of their earlier Writ Petitions in which rule 7 was held to be mandatorily applicable, the Petitioners cannot now be permitted a dramatic volte face and allowed to submit successfully that the Court did not take this issue into consideration in delivering the Judgment dated 16-3-2006. That line of argument as offered by Mr. Mohammed Mutahar Hossain without further cogent reason or explanation does not make any sense to this Court and, as such, the Petitioners having previously not raised any question on this issue at the material time to challenge the sufficiencies of that earlier Judgment are now found to be estopped from raising it before this Court. Consequentially it is this Court's finding that the Petitioners have no locus standi to challenge the vires of rule 8 by way of judicial review. 

 32. Relying upon the second limb of the Rule Nisi issued in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 the Writ Petitioners have sought a direction upon the Respondents to provide them 7th Selection Grade under article 7(7) of the জাতীয় বেতন স্কেল, ২০০৯ ("National Pay Scale, 2009") by counting their tenure of service of the development projects from the date of joining in their respective development projects and not from their dates of regularization in the year 2010 which ultimately means that by making such prayer the Petitioners indirectly claim seniority from their dates of joining in the development projects. Mr. MA. Gaffar in representing the Respondents points out significantly that the Petitioners being regularized in the year 2010 came before this Court through this Writ Petition in the year 2014 to get 7th Grade Selection Grade where they need only 4 years length of service in the revenue budget which already they had at the time of filing of this Writ Petition and since then they have completed more than 10 years of service in the revenue budget post and, as such, no direction is at all necessary from the court for counting/including their development project service after being 10 years in the revenue budget to cover 4 years period to get 7th Selection Grade under article 7(7) and on this ground alone the Rule may be discharged for being not maintainable. 

 33. In considering Mr. MA. Gaffar's submissions above it is noted by this Court that Selection Grade according to article 7(7) of the National Pay Scale. 2009 is given on the basis of seniority. According to condition "Ka" of the Petitioner's appointment order their seniority will be counted from their date of regularization (“নিয়মিতকরণের আদেশ জারীর তারিখ হতে কর্মকর্তাগণের জ্যেষ্ঠতা গণনা করা হবে।)i.e., from 5-10-2010 which has indeed not been challenged by them. Rather by accepting this condition in condition "Ka" the Petitioners were in the facts regularized in the revenue budget and, as such, at this juncture this Court finds that there is no scope to grant selection grade under article 7(7) of the National Pay Scale, 2009 by counting service beyond the date of their regularization. Furthermore, to condition "Kha" of their appointment order as states that আদেশ জারীর পূর্বে এলজিইডির সাংগঠনিক কাঠামো ভুক্ত রাজস্ব খাতের সহকারী প্রকৌশলী/উিপজেলা সহকারী প্রকৌশলী পদে নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োজিত প্রকৌশলীগণের পরে অত্র আদেশ ছারা নিয়মিত কর্মকর্তাদের জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হবে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ হবে has been inserted therein to clearly mean that the Petitioners being evidently 5 years junior to the Added Respondents and many others cannot get 7th Selection Grade under article 7(7) of the National Pay Scale, 2009 by taking into account their tenure of the service period of development projects as otherwise prayed for here inasmuch as in that case if the Petitioners' length of service is counted from the date of their joining in the development projects the Added Respondents and others similarly placed Senior Assistant Engineers in spite of being 5-15 years senior will automatically become junior to the Petitioners. This Court, accordingly, finds that Selection Grade under article 7(7) is given on the basis of seniority and, as such, it is simply impossible to make the Rule absolute as prayed for. Such finding of this Court is further based on an additional legal bar in counting the service period of development projects of the Petitioners beyond their date of regularization. That bar is evident in rule 5 of the Rules 2005 upon which the Petitioner's have relied themselves. Rule 5 also imposes a legal bar as follows: জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ-(১) এই বিধিমালার অধীনে নিয়মিত কৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণের ক্ষেত্রে তার নিয়মিত করণের তারিখ হতে গণনা করা হবে। Therefore, this Court finds that there is also a legal bar under the Rules 2005 to grant selection grade under article 7(7) as prayed by the Petitioners by counting this service beyond this date of regularization. 

 34. With regard to the Judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 8983 of 2011 as well as the Judgment dated 10-4-2013 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 308 of 2013 it is submitted by Mr. M.A. Gaffar for the Added Respondents that these are not applicable in the present case of the Petitioners who are Class 1 officers and were admittedly appointed under special circumstances under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 by relaxation of certain provisions as stated and considered above and in the manner as those earlier regularized 95 Assistant Engineers who accepted their entitled service benefits by counting their service from their date of regularization dated 28-7-2004 and, as such, the Petitioners being at par with those 95 Engineers cannot be treated presently as an exception. This Court finds considerable merit in that line of argument. On the other hand, the beneficiaries of the Judgment in Writ Petition No. 8983 of 2011 are Class II and III employees who sought to be regularized under the Rules 2005 after completion of the tenure of their projects and, accordingly, were regularized under the Rules 2005. Significantly further, in the said Writ Petition the question of applicability of the Rules 1995, Rules 2005, LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 or the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 were not in question and, as such, the present Petitioners being admittedly and evidently appointed/regularized under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 like the Added Respondents are not similarly situated as those earlier Writ Petitioners and, as such, are not entitled to get any benefit of the said Judgment in Writ Petition No. 8983 of 2011. 

 35. This Court's findings above lead indisputably to the conclusion that the Added Respondents are senior in service to the Petitioners. By that reason, if the present Rule Nisi is made absolute by ignoring the accepted conditions "Ka" and "Kha" of the Appointment Notification dated 5-10-2010 and the legal bars under rule 5 of the Rules 2005 and the question of seniority involved in providing Selection Grade under article 7(7) of the জাতীয় বেতন স্কেল, ২০০৯ or National Pay Scale, 2009 which provides “ক্যাডার ১ নন ক্যাডার নির্বিশেষে ৯ম গ্রেড ভুক্ত সকল ১ম শ্রেনীর কর্মকর্তাকে ৪ চোর) বখসর চাকরিচ্যুত, সন্তোষজনক চাকরির রেকর্ড ও জ্যেষ্ঠতার ভিত্তিতে এতদ্সংক্রান্ত প্রচলিত শর্তাদি পুরণ সাপেক্ষে ৭ম গ্রেডের ফেলে ৫০% সিলেকশন গ্রেড প্রদানের পরিবর্তে জাতীয় বেতন ক্কেল ২০০৯ অনুযায়ী ১ জুলাই ২০০৯ হইতে ১০০% সিলেকশন গ্রেড প্রদেয় হইবে" and, as such, if Selection Grade is provided to the Petitioners by counting their service from their date of joining in the development projects as prayed by them, then in view of article 7(7) of the National Pay Scale, 2009 the Added Respondents and hundreds of other similarly placed officers appointed through PSC by demonstrating their talent will automatically become junior in contravention of their fundamental rights under articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution as well and the same will be against the thrust and ethos of articles 19 and 20 of the Fundamental Principles of State Policy and there will be a serious administrative disorder in all the Government departments. Let all concerned pay heed to this finding and observation by this Court. 

 36. Considering the above, this Court, accordingly, finds no merit in the Petitioners' Application in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 and no substance in the Rule issued. Resultantly, the Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 is, hereby, discharged. The Order of restraint as initially issued is necessarily, hereby, recalled and vacated. 

 38. That standpoint is reinforced by the Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 295 of 2015 in which the Petitioners there have challenged rule 6 of SRO 182 “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫ or the Determination of Regularisation and Seniority of Personnel Transferred/Absorbed from Development Project to Revenue Head Rules (already previously defined as "the Rules 2005") as being vague and contradictory and totally unclear provision included in the SRO dated 20-5-2005 which conflicts with articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution. The Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 295 of 2015 have also sought a declaration that the said SRO 182 dated 20-6-2005 has been wrongly applied in respect of Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and other similarly situated Engineers appointed under LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 vide order dated 5-10-2010 and they are not entitled to any benefit there under. 

 40. The Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 were also earlier appointed under development projects in 1992 and 1993 but having failed to enter in the service of the revenue budget through PSC remained in the development projects and subsequently relying on a special case of regularization of previously regularized 95 Assistant Engineers vide Notification dated 28-7-2004 they along with many others filed Writ Petitions before this Court by relying upon the said Notification dated 28-7-2004 for being absorbed in the same way as has been done in case of those 95 Assistant Engineers. Their prayers to that effect were allowed and they were absorbed by operation of the Judgment dated 16-3-2006 by appointment Notification dated 5-10-2010 under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 in the manner as those 95 Assistant Engineers. Those 95 Assistant Engineers were regularized in the year 2004 under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 by specifically relaxing rule 4(1), 4(3) and 4(4) and column 3 of the Schedule of the LGED Recruitment Rule, 1986 under special consideration for one time only on humanitarian ground. These are facts that have already been visited by this Court in the course of disposing of the Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 8513 of 2014 above. 

 41. A vital issue involved in this Writ Petition is that how the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 being appointed/regularized under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009 in the same way as those earlier regularized 95 Assistant Engineers are receiving higher salary than the Petitioners though they are 4/5 years senior in service to Respondent Nos. 8 and 9. The Petitioners were appointed in the year 2005/2006 and the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 in the year 2010 but the Respondents No. 8 and 9 and other similarly placed Assistant Engineers are getting higher salaries upon misapplication of rule 6 of SRO 182, i.e., Rules 2005 and they are continuously and illegally taking benefit of it. Resultantly, the Petitioners being senior in service and being similarly situated in so far their entry into the revenue budget of the LGED is concerned have been seriously discriminated due to an anomaly created by rule 6 contrary to Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution and are being deprived of their legal rights to get equal protection of law so far their salaries are concerned. This Court accepts the Petitioners' contention that rule 6 of the SRO 182 i.e., the Rules 2005 being vague, contradictory, discriminatory and devoid of objective standards of classification and application is ultra vires the Constitution to the extent of its beneficial application in favour of the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and others similarly placed and that as such the same is not applicable in respect of the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and others similarly placed Assistant Engineers appointed vide Notification dated 5-10-2010. Predicated on the above this Court finds further that rule 6 of SRO 182 is being consistently misused and misapplied in favour of those who came from development projects given that it suffers from an inherent lack of clarity and vagueness and it is not consequentially clear why in respect of salary etc. past service of the development employees should be counted after being absorbed in the revenue budget. By that reason, and in acceptance of the submissions of the Petitioners' learned Advocate Mr. MA. Gaffar this Court holds that rule 6 of the Rules 2005 is indeed discriminatory and, therefore, ultra vires the Constitution in so far as its beneficial application to the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and others similarly appointed on 5-10-2010. Consequentially, it is this Court's finding that rule 6 can henceforth have no manner of application as enures to the benefit of the Respondent Nos. 8 and 9 and other similarly placed Assistant Engineers appointed under the LGED Recruitment Rules, 1986 or the LGED Recruitment Rules, 2009. In addressing further the Rule Nisi as issued an its totality, this Court further finds that all pecuniary and financial benefit that have accrued to Respondent No. 8 and 9 and others similarly placed by invocation of rule 6 to their benefit have so accrued without any legal basis. Consequentially, it now becomes imperative particularly for the Respondent No. 1, Secretary LGED, to examine this particular aspect and devise a mechanism in accordance with law to ensure the realization from the Respondent No. 8 and 9 and others similarly placed of excess public money in the form of similar and benefits that have been paid them since their appointment on 5-10-2010. After all, public money ought not to be dispensed with such largesse to anyone without due sanction of law and sound reason.
